question.text: What obligation does an option seller (writer) have in an exchange-traded IRO?

answer.text: To fulfill the contract obligation if the buyer exercises the option, backed by margin deposited with the exchange
No obligation once the premium is received
To exercise the option on behalf of the buyer
To return the premium if the option expires ITM

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook explains that the option seller receives the premium for assuming the obligation, can be assigned if the buyer exercises, and is subject to short-option margin requirements at the exchange. The Trap: Receiving the premium does not extinguish the writer's obligation -- it persists until expiry or until the position is closed. The writer does not exercise (only the buyer can), and the premium is never returned to the buyer. Note: Short-option positions specifically attract margin (including extreme loss margin), reflecting the writer's open obligation.
